paper.title_en: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
paper.abstract_en: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations. The $K-χ$ relation displays two distinct linear regimes separated near $T^\ast\approx 250$ K, with different slopes indicating a change in the effective transferred hyperfine couplings. Below $T_{N}$, the relaxation follows $1/T_1\propto T^5$, consistent with magnon-mediated relaxation in the ordered state. The temperature dependence of the internal hyperfine field yields a critical exponent $β\approx 0.36$, consistent with three-dimensional universality. Together, these results establish AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ as a quasi-one-dimensional $S=3/2$ antiferromagnet embedded in a layered van der Waals host, in which local probes directly resolve the crossover from correlated intrachain spin dynamics to anisotropic three-dimensional magnetic order. More broadly, AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a useful van der Waals platform for studying dimensional crossover, correlated spin dynamics, and hyperfine-coupling evolution in low-dimensional antiferromagnets.
